title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Asha Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document codifies Redwood Inference’s standard processes and manager responsibilities for hiring, new-employee onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle. It is intended for people-ops partners, hiring managers, interviewers, and people managers across engineering, product, and GTM functions.

Scope
- Full lifecycle: requisition -> hire -> onboarding -> ongoing performance management
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors on >6 month engagements, and interns unless a role-specific policy overrides these steps.

Owner and escalation
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood-inference.com)
- Escalation: Head of People Ops -> VP People -> Legal (if employment/immigration/offer terms)

---

1) Hiring process (standard requisition flow)

Summary
A clear, consistent hiring process improves candidate experience, reduces time-to-fill, and ensures equitable evaluation. The canonical stages are: Requisition -> Sourcing -> Screen -> Onsite / Loop -> Offer -> Close. Aim time-to-offer (engineering IC roles): 28 calendar days from requisition to offer for typical roles; escalate extended searches to talent partner.

Requisition (Manager + People Ops)
- Manager creates req in Workday with role template and level.
- People Ops reviews JD, salary band, EEO language, and approves posting.
- Required artifacts before posting: scorecard (see below), interview panel slate, hiring timeline.

Sourcing & screen
- Sourcing owns outbound outreach; hiring manager schedules a 30-min phone screen (or take-home assessment where applicable).
- First screen evaluates fit on 3 dimensions: core skills, role motivation, and compensation/availability. Use the standard screen template:
  1. Tell me about your recent work relevant to this role.
  2. Why Redwood and what would excite you in this role?
  3. Basic technical/role question to assess baseline competency.
  4. Availability and compensation expectations.
- Score with the simple green/amber/red rubric and capture notes in the ATS.

Interview loop (panel)
- Minimum panel composition: hiring manager, senior peer, cross-functional partner (product/infra/customer-facing), and a people-ops or recruiter observer for calibration.
- Typical loop length: 3-4 interviews of 45-60 minutes each, covering: role-specific skills, system design / product sense (as applicable), behavioral / culture fit, collaboration & communication.
- Use the role scorecard to map which interviewer assesses which competencies.

Decision & calibration
- Hiring manager collates scores and notes. People Ops runs a quick calibration (within 48 hours) for roles at director+ or salary band exceptions.
- Decision rubric: Hire if 75%+ interviewers rated green on core competencies OR a clear growth plan exists and team bandwidth to mentor.

Offer & closing
- People Ops drafts offer using approved comp band and benefit language. Manager confirms role, start date, and any relocation/visa needs.
- Standard turnaround: extend verbal offer same day if approvals complete; written offer within 24 business hours.
- For declined offers, capture candidate feedback and update pipeline; if counter-offer risk is high, consult People Ops.

Hiring metrics to track
- Time-to-offer, acceptance rate, diversity of interview slate, interview-to-offer conversion, and source-of-hire ROI.

---

2) Interviewer guidelines & scorecard (short reference)

Interviewer expectations
- Be on time, prepared, and review the candidate’s materials beforehand.
- Ask behavioral questions based on past work; probe for concrete outcomes and trade-offs.
- Focus on evidence: concrete examples, scope of ownership, constraints, and impact.
- Commit a score and written rationale within 24 hours.

Scorecard (simple canonical version)
- Competency buckets (each rated Green / Amber / Red and comment required):
  - Role proficiency (technical/functional)
  - Problem solving & judgment
  - Collaboration & communication
  - Ownership & execution
  - Team fit & culture add
- Hiring manager: aggregate and determine next step.

Bias mitigation & inclusive interviewing
- Use structured questions from the scorecard.
- Avoid hypotheticals that rely on privileged experiences.
- People Ops can anonymize resumes for early-stage screens on request.

---

3) Offer templates and candidate communications

Standard elements in offer letter
- Role title and level, manager, start date, base salary, target bonus (if applicable), equity grant summary, benefits summary, primary location and remote policy expectations, at-will employment language, background check & immigration contingencies.

Quick email template (verbal offer)
Hi [Candidate Name],

We’d like to extend an offer to join Redwood Inference as a [Role]. We’ll follow up with a written offer that includes full details, but the high-level terms are [base, equity, target start date]. Please let us know if you have questions and whether you’d like more time to consider.

Best,
[Hiring Manager] + People Ops

---

4) New hire onboarding (Day 0 -> 90)

Principles
- First impressions matter: remove administrative friction and provide a role-focused ramp.
- Ensure equipment, access, and clear first-month goals before start.
- Managers are accountable for the 30/60/90 plan and first-week check-ins.

Preboarding (1-2 weeks before start)
- People Ops actions: send welcome packet (benefits, first-week agenda), collect tax/eligibility docs, and schedule HR orientation.
- IT actions: order laptop & peripherals; create accounts (Google, Slack, Confluence, Okta, internal tools), add to team repos and calendar groups.
- Manager actions: send an intro email to the team, schedule 1:1 cadence, prepare 30/60/90 draft and first-week onboarding tasks.

Day 1 checklist
- HR orientation & benefits enrollment session (People Ops)
- Manager-led welcome (team intro, role overview, and immediate priorities)
- IT verification: VPN, SSO, internal repos, and access to project trackers
- Assign a peer buddy for first 30 days

Week 1 (goal: context & connectivity)
- Meet the team: product, engineering, SRE, customer success as applicable
- Shadow sessions: product demos, support queue walk-through, codebase orientation
- Deliverable: small onboarding task with review (e.g., fix a minor bug, update doc, or ship a one-pager)

Month 1 (goal: contribution & clarity)
- Manager 1:1 weekly; People Ops check-in at week 4
- Review 30-day deliverable and iterate on 60/90 plan
- Ensure performance calibration goal set and success metrics documented

30/60/90 plan template (manager editable)
- 30 days: learn systems, meet stakeholders, complete onboarding tasks
- 60 days: contribute to a larger project, lead a small cross-functional discussion
- 90 days: deliver a feature/initiative end-to-end and demonstrate ownership

Remote-specific notes
- Schedule overlapping hours and weekly virtual coffee with buddy
- Ship welcome kit and local tax/benefit country guidance prior to start

---

5) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and overview
- Continuous feedback is primary. Formal cycles: quarterly check-ins and an annual performance review. For ICs, compensation reviews are annual with mid-year calibrations.
- Managers are required to give written quarterly check-ins and to document goals in the Goals sheet.

Quarterly check-ins
- Short written summary: accomplishments, blockers, updated goals, development priorities.
- Manager and direct report should discuss at least once per quarter in a dedicated 30-60 minute meeting.

Annual review process
- Timeline: calibration meeting in November; written reviews finalized by mid-December; compensation recommendations due by year-end.
- Steps: self-assessment -> manager assessment -> peer feedback where applicable -> calibration -> final rating & comp decision -> manager-delivered conversation.
- Rating scale (4-point simplified): Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Developing / Does Not Meet.

Calibration & moderation
- Calibration meetings grouped by function to ensure consistent standards for level expectations and comp bands. People Ops facilitates and ensures no systemic bias in distributions.

Promotion & leveling
- Promotions: initiated by manager with evidence (impact, scope increase, mentorship, cross-team influence). Submit promotion packet to People Ops with examples and peer references. Promotions typically align with review cycles but can occur off-cycle for clear cases.

Performance improvement (PIP)
- PIP steps: documented performance concerns -> agreed corrective plan with measurable objectives and timeline (30-90 days) -> manager check-ins weekly -> HR/People Ops oversight -> post-PIP outcome: successful, extended, or separation.
- Managers must involve People Ops before issuing a PIP to ensure fairness and documentation completeness.

Reward & recognition
- Use the peer-nominated Kudos program for immediate recognition; quarterly awards and spot bonuses are discretionary and routed through People Ops.

---

6) Manager responsibilities (summary checklist)

Hiring
- Create/own the req, prepare scorecard, interview actively, and close offers in partnership with People Ops.

Onboarding
- Complete preboarding checklist, own 30/60/90 plan, assign buddy, schedule regular 1:1s, and ensure ramp outcomes.

Performance management
- Provide regular feedback, document quarterly check-ins, run calibration prep, and initiate promotion or PIP processes with evidence.

Career development
- Own career conversations, set clear success metrics, support stretch assignments, and provide sponsorship opportunities.

Compliance & administration
- Ensure required trainings are completed (security, code of conduct) and approvals for headcount/spending are in place.

---

7) Templates & examples (copy-paste resources)

- 30/60/90 Plan (example)
  - 30: Read docs, meet 10 stakeholders, complete onboarding ticket A
  - 60: Ship feature B with review, own on-call rotation shadowing
  - 90: Lead rollout of named capability and measure KPI improvements

- Quarterly check-in email template
  Hi [Name],

  For this quarter I wanted to highlight the following accomplishments: [list].
  Development priorities for next quarter: [list].
  Can we meet on [date] to discuss?

  Thanks,
  [Manager]

- PIP starter template (manager to People Ops)
  - Concern summary, evidence (dates/examples), expected outcomes, success metrics, timeline, and support plan.

---

8) FAQs & common scenarios

- Q: What if a candidate asks for an above-band offer?
  A: Escalate to People Ops. We allow limited flexibility for critical hires and must document the business case for approvals.

- Q: When should I open an off-cycle promotion?
  A: Off-cycle promotions are for exceptional impact; consult People Ops first. Most promotions follow the annual review unless there is a strong business need.

- Q: How do we handle extended onboarding for senior hires?
  A: Build an individualized ramp plan, schedule stakeholder introductions ahead of start, and budget for 60-90 day enablement resources. People Ops will coordinate executive briefings.
